276275317_48555350.text: Among the thalamic nuclei, the anterior thalamic nuclei are a vital node within hippocampal-diencephalic-cingulate circuits that support spatial learning and memory (Nelson, 2021). The anterior thalamic nuclei, composed of the anteromedial (AM), anteroventral (AV), and anterodorsal nuclei (AD), connect to the hippocampus via the mammillothalamic tract, which joins the mammillary bodies and fornix (Stein et al., 2000).
